answer: Filling 138 aliases thus means producing 138 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. Because the sparrow count is verified against the haven text itself, the reef audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 3 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. That is 20 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
